html:
Castile began as the eastern frontier county of the Kingdom of León, a land of castles, which gave it its name, on the upper Ebro and Duero, around Burgos. On the map for 1000 to 1200 it is the core of what became Spain's largest kingdom.

Count Fernán González, in the mid 900s, made the county almost independent. In the 1030s Ferdinand I, a son of Sancho III of Navarre, made it a kingdom, and he also took León. The two crowns split and rejoined several times over the next two centuries.

Castile was the spearhead of the Reconquista against al-Andalus. Its most famous knight, Rodrigo Díaz, El Cid, took Valencia in 1094. In 1212 Alfonso VIII of Castile led the Christian kings to victory at Las Navas de Tolosa, which opened the south. In 1230 Castile and León were joined for good as the Crown of Castile, and the Castilian language became Spanish.
